items.title: UK-Iranian Man Arrested in Connection to RAF Fairford Air Base Incident
items.summary: British police said a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national was arrested Thursday. British officials have said they believe Iran played a part in planning the incident at R.A.F. Fairford.

items.title: Investigators Seek to Establish Motive in FlyDubai Attack
items.summary: The United Arab Emirates said it would lead the investigation, including into possible links to terrorism. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel said the attacker had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination,” though he did not elaborate.

items.title: Canada’s Proposed Oil Pipeline Offers Carney Relief From Domestic and Global Turmoil
items.summary: The new pipeline from Alberta’s oil sands to the Pacific Coast may lower separatist tensions in that province while also loosening energy ties with the U.S.

items.title: Nigerian Charged With Running Fake Government Agency
items.summary: The Nigerian secured office space in a federal building, opened bank accounts and even held meetings with foreign diplomats. He says he is innocent.

items.title: Egypt Arrests 6 Matsaddash Journalists on Claims of Spreading Disinformation
items.summary: The government claims that reporters from Matsaddash, a well-known news outlet that debunks false reports, spread disinformation for the banned Muslim Brotherhood.

items.title: American University of Afghanistan at Risk of Closure Amid Funding Cuts
items.summary: The State Department has denied its funding for the next two years, jeopardizing the education of hundreds of female Afghan students.

items.title: Russia to Sharply Increase War Spending and Cut Social Programs
items.summary: Both sides are finding it increasingly difficult to finance the conflict in Ukraine. Russia’s 2027 budget envisions more debt, higher taxes and lower social benefits.

items.title: Finnish Lawmakers Report Suspicious Home Break-Ins
items.summary: The speaker of Parliament said there were a “considerable” number of mysterious entries in which perpetrators appeared to have taken nothing.

items.title: A Flashy Zimbabwean Tycoon Who Befriended Presidents Dies in Crash
items.summary: Wicknell Chivayo was riding in a helicopter with his wife when it plunged into a field. Dogged by corruption allegations, the businessman drew polarizing reactions even in death.

items.title: Who Is Captain Smit Machchhar, the Pilot Hailed as a Hero After FlyDubai Cockpit Stabbing?
items.summary: Capt. Smit Machchhar suffered stab wounds while fending off an attack from his co-pilot, saving the lives of around 170 people on board, officials said.

items.title: David Ellison’s Vision for CNN: Same C.E.O and No Bari Weiss, for Now.
items.summary: David Ellison is negotiating to keep CNN’s chief executive, Mark Thompson, in place without oversight from Bari Weiss, the CBS editor in chief, when the networks’ parent companies merge.

items.title: US Sanctions A7, a Russia Firm That Helps Sidestep Economic Restrictions
items.summary: The move follows recent reports detailing how A7, a Russian financial firm, used shell companies around the world to move funds on behalf of restricted Russian businesses.

items.title: What to Know About Trump Accounts as More Than 60 Million Children Are Auto-Enrolled
items.summary: The Trump administration may have just signed up your child — and more than 60 million others — for a 530A savings account (if you haven’t already done so).

items.title: Swedish Company Uses A.I. Likeness of Greta Garbo in Ad
items.summary: An ad produced by the manufacturing company SKF Group featured a digital version of the Swedish American actress, who died in 1990. Not all viewers found the replica convincing.

items.title: As Mortgage Rates Hit Highest Level Since 2023, Buyers Look at ARMs
items.summary: The average 30-year, fixed-rate home loan rose to 7.28 percent, up from 6.34 percent a year ago. More buyers are now turning to adjustable-rate mortgages.

items.title: Trump’s Threat to Ban Diesel Exports Sets Off Global Alarms
items.summary: A reduction in refineries has already driven the price of diesel to record highs, threatening economies. An U.S. export ban would be “tremendous shock and blow.”

items.title: Federal Watchdog Investigates Adam Kinzinger for Kalshi Bets on His Pardon
items.summary: The inquiry by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission centers on bets the former congressman made on Kalshi in the weeks before he was pardoned in January 2025.

items.title: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
items.summary: The higher yields, which are pressuring consumer and corporate borrowers and increasingly weighing on certain corners of the stock market, are unlikely to dissipate soon.

items.title: The Global Bond Rout Reaches Worrying New Levels
items.summary: Investors are on alert as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note hit a new multi-decade high. The sell-off is also broadening in Europe, too.

items.title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
items.summary: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Who’s to Blame When A.I. Goes Rogue?
items.summary: Many think artificial intelligence companies should be held liable for their runaway technology. But legal scholars say applying existing law could be messy

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
items.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

items.title: Amazon Settles Lawsuit Over Claims of Slow Deliveries to Low-Income Areas
items.summary: The tech giant will refund $7.25 million in Prime membership fees to affected customers and pay an additional $1 million to settle the suit brought by the District of Columbia.

items.title: What’s Next for ‘Hard Fork’?
items.summary: The podcast’s next chapter begins this week.

items.title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.
items.summary: An unusual study aims to estimate the pollution and health costs from a cluster of proposed data centers, instead of considering each one separately.

items.title: Google Releases New Gemini Model With Guardrails Amid A.I. Safety Debate
items.summary: For safety reasons, Gemini 4 Argon will initially be available only to some companies and organizations focused on cybersecurity defense before it is more widely released, Google said.

items.title: F.T.C. Investigates OpenAI and Anthropic Over Potential Consumer Harms
items.summary: The agency will examine whether A.I. labs have broken federal laws prohibiting companies from unfair and deceptive practices.
